research_page.title: Verubecestat in mild-to-moderate AD (EPOCH)
research_page.description: A pivotal Phase 2/3 trial of the BACE-1 inhibitor verubecestat that was terminated early for futility, showing no clinical benefit despite lowering amyloid.
research_page.authors_line_md: Michael F. Egan et al. — Merck
research_page.takeaway_md: The BACE-1 inhibitor verubecestat effectively reduced amyloid-beta production but failed to slow cognitive or functional decline in a large, rigorous trial of mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease. The study was terminated early for futility and highlighted significant adverse events associated with the drug. This high-quality evidence contributed heavily to the abandonment of the BACE-1 inhibitor class for symptomatic Alzheimer's.
key_findings_md: The trial was terminated early for futility at 50 months, finding no significant difference in cognitive (ADAS-cog) or functional (ADCS-ADL) decline between verubecestat and placebo (paper, Abstract).
Verubecestat successfully reduced cerebrospinal fluid Aβ-40 and Aβ-42 by over 60% and modestly lowered brain amyloid load (paper, RESULTS / BIOMARKERS).
Patients on verubecestat experienced higher rates of adverse events, including falls, sleep disturbances, weight loss, suicidal ideation, and hair color changes (paper, RESULTS / SAFETY).
research_page.methods_md: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 78-week Phase 2/3 trial evaluating verubecestat (12 mg or 40 mg daily) versus placebo. The study randomized 1,958 patients aged 55 to 85 with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease and was registered as NCT01739348.
research_page.trial_evidence_md: This document reports on the pivotal EPOCH trial ([NCT01739348](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01739348)), which conclusively demonstrated the drug's futility in a mild-to-moderate population. (Note: The registry lists 2,211 enrolled patients versus the paper's 1,958 randomized, reflecting standard screen failures). A subsequent Phase 3 trial in prodromal patients, APECS ([NCT01953601](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01953601)), was also terminated early for futility, leading to the complete abandonment of the verubecestat clinical program.
research_page.sentiment_md: Public and scientific perception of verubecestat shifted from early hype over its potent plaque-clearing ability to profound disappointment following its trial failures. Today, the drug is primarily discussed in scientific forums (like Alzforum and r/science) as a definitive cautionary tale about the disconnect between amyloid clearance and clinical benefit, as well as the specific toxicities and cognitive worsening associated with the BACE inhibitor class.
caveats_md: The trial did not mandate amyloid biomarker confirmation for enrollment; although a substudy suggested roughly 90% positivity, a small portion of the cohort likely had non-amyloid dementia.

BACE-1 inhibitors like verubecestat have since demonstrated class-wide toxicities and cognitive worsening, meaning the adverse events may have masked any potential neuroprotective benefits of amyloid reduction.
relates_to_md: [Amyloid hypothesis](/research/amyloid-hypothesis) — The clinical failure of verubecestat despite successful target engagement posed a major challenge to the amyloid cascade hypothesis.
[Randomized Trial of Verubecestat for Prodromal Alzheimer’s Disease](/research/papers/verubecestat-apecs) — The related Phase 3 APECS trial in earlier-stage patients, which also failed.

trial_pages.title: EPOCH: Verubecestat in mild-to-moderate AD
trial_pages.description: A Phase 2/3 trial evaluating the BACE-1 inhibitor verubecestat in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease, terminated early for futility.
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in ADAS-Cog and ADCS-ADL scores at week 78
trial_pages.why_md: This trial tested whether blocking the production of amyloid-beta via BACE-1 inhibition could slow clinical decline in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease. Its high-profile failure raised significant questions about the [amyloid hypothesis](/research/amyloid-hypothesis) and the timing of therapeutic intervention.
status_log_md: **2017-02-15** — Trial terminated early for futility following an independent data monitoring committee recommendation.
trial_pages.results_md: The trial found no significant differences in cognitive or functional decline between verubecestat and placebo after 78 weeks. While verubecestat effectively reduced cerebrospinal fluid amyloid-beta, it was associated with higher rates of adverse events, including falls, rash, sleep disturbances, suicidal ideation, and weight loss.

timeline_entries.title: 2017-02 — Verubecestat EPOCH trial terminated for futility
timeline_entries.body_md: Merck halts its Phase 2/3 EPOCH trial of the BACE-1 inhibitor verubecestat in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's after an independent committee finds no chance of clinical benefit, marking a major setback for the BACE inhibitor class. [Read the EPOCH results](/research/papers/verubecestat-epoch).

notes_for_editor: The registry lists 2,211 enrolled patients while the paper reports 1,958 randomized; this has been noted in the trial_evidence_md section to explain the discrepancy.
